title: U-net skip connections (modded-nanogpt): learned-scalar skips from blocks 0-2 outputs into blocks 5-3 inputs, on the 107-claude Peri-LN Lean incumbent (4,800,003 params)
description: New mechanism, not from the P-list (closest: P10 reinjection and P38 early-value residual, applied to a non-looped model): the fork GPT forward gains modded-nanogpt's U-net skips, adding the output of block i (i<3) scaled by a learned scalar (init 1) to the input of block 5-i. In a Peri-LN stream every block writes a unit-RMS vector, so early token-level features (exact symbols and names needed to copy cited formulas) are diluted by later writes; the skips let the last blocks re-read them, which should help the RL policy stay precise on longer (>=7-line) proofs than pretraining shows.
hypothesis: Val loss saturates at ~0.082 by ~200 s on every Lean run (100-112 curves flat from 225 s), so pretraining fit is not what separates runs; the RL outcome depends on how the solution generalizes to longer proofs. Late layers that can directly read early, token-identity-rich activations (instead of a stream where they are ~1/10 of the variance after 10 unit Peri-LN writes) should copy premises and names more exactly as sequences grow past pretraining lengths, raising round-1 targets solved and cutting Lean parse failures; the skip scalars cost no measurable step time.
expected_delta: -40 to +40 dev solves >= 7 vs 107-claude's 587.00 (central 0); pretraining steps within 2% of 107's 3,208-3,277, final val loss 0.079-0.086; totals 1,850-2,150 s, under the 2,400 s cap

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with Peri-LN blocks (107-claude) and U-net skip connections between the first and last three blocks (UNetGPT subclass)
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN; unchanged from 107-claude)
arch.change: CHANGED vs 107-claude: only the GPT forward. UNetGPT(GPT) adds skip_weights = nn.Parameter(ones(3)); forward is the fork's GPT.forward (same rope_cache/pos/mask/caches handling) except that the outputs of blocks 0,1,2 are pushed on a stack and, before blocks 3,4,5, x = x + skip_weights[i-3] * stack.pop(), i.e. block 3 input += w0*out2 (a pure rescale of the stream, as in modded-nanogpt), block 4 input += w1*out1, block 5 input += w2*out0. Blocks, widths, init and RNG draws are identical to 107 (skip weights init 1 without RNG)
arch.skip_weights: 3 scalars, init 1.0, in the AdamW auxiliary group (lr 1e-3, wd 0.1, same schedule); persist into RL (frozen RL AdamW trains them like every other parameter)
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: UNetGPT(vocab, 6, 256, 8) from pretrain.py, replace blocks with PeriLNBlock, load state (state dict = 107's plus skip_weights)
arch.kv_cache: fork attention/cache code unchanged; skips add same-call, same-position activations, so cached decoding equals the full forward (CPU check: prefill 5 tokens with causal mask then 7 single-token cached steps vs one full forward, skip weights set to (0.7,1.3,-0.4): max |logit diff| 9.5e-7)

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude except the orthogonalization polynomial)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f) as in 107-claude, CHANGED: + UNetGPT.skip_weights (3 scalars, same lr 1e-3 / wd 0.1); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW
optimizer.parameters: unchanged from 101-claude: 24 hidden matrices (6 x qkv.weight (768,256) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)

config.init: Fork default construction (normal 0.02 embedding/readout), blocks replaced by PeriLNBlocks and re-initialized with the fork _init (zero biases), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); output LayerNorms gain 1, bias 0 (standard Peri-LN / OLMo 2 / Gemma 2 init). RNG draws shift vs 101-claude because the blocks are built twice. At init each branch write has RMS ~1 instead of ~0.1. 114: identical to 107 (same RNG draws); skip_weights init 1.0 without RNG
